method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)' (first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026), 22 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (eviQ 'Disclaimer and copyright' page: 'Information on the eviQ website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 license (CC BY-NC 4.0)'). eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites; adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page, fetched 2026-09-24)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)' (first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (eviQ 'Disclaimer and copyright' page: 'Information on the eviQ website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 license (CC BY-NC 4.0)'). eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites; adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page, fetched 2026-09-24)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Source page fetched 2026-09-24 and converted from HTML to text; eviQ tables (dose levels, trial results) survive as text on this page and are anchored where used. Edition 2.0 keeps every S1 (eviQ 4506 belzutifan) claim unchanged and adds S2, the separate eviQ cancer-genetics risk-management page for VHL (ID 397, version 11, aligned with the 2023 International VHL Surveillance Guidelines Consortium and VHL Alliance), paraphrased because it is CC BY-NC; its surveillance tables survive as text and are anchored.

claims.claim: **VHL is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait and predisposes to clear cell kidney cancer, phaeochromocytoma, and haemangioblastomas of the retina and central nervous system;** about 20% of people have a new (de novo) variant.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Approximate lifetime frequency (mean age at onset):** retinal angioma 49-62% (25), cerebellar haemangioblastoma 60-80% (30), kidney cancer 40-70% (40), phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma 10-20% (24), pancreatic NET 8-17% (35), endolymphatic sac tumour 6-15% (30).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Parents, siblings and children each have up to a 50% chance of carrying the variant;** relatives should be referred for predictive testing at a familial cancer centre or genetics service.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Kidney and pancreas: abdominal MRI every 2 years from age 15.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Phaeochromocytoma:** a yearly examination including blood pressure from age 2, and from age 5 yearly fasting plasma free metanephrines, with plasma 3-methoxytyramine where available (24-hour urinary metanephrines if plasma testing is not possible).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Brain and spine haemangioblastoma: MRI of brain and spine every 2 years from age 11. Retina: paediatric review at birth, then a yearly eye review from age 1.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Endolymphatic sac tumour: hearing tests every 2 years from age 11, plus one high-resolution MRI of the internal auditory canals between 15 and 20** (or at diagnosis for anyone diagnosed after 20). Early detection and surgery can save hearing.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Surveillance is the same for all VHL genotypes** (links between VHL subtype and tumour pattern are not yet reliable enough to tailor it), and routine nuclear scans are of uncertain value. Epididymal cystadenomas need no routine surveillance.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **When to stop:** blood tests and imaging may cease in someone without symptoms who reaches 65 with no VHL lesions on earlier screening, but yearly examination and eye checks continue.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Kidney tumours are often multiple and bilateral. Watch renal masses under 3 cm with MRI (active surveillance),** and manage kidney cancer in a unit experienced in VHL and nephron-sparing surgery.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pancreatic cysts are the commonest pancreatic finding and are essentially never malignant;** follow them and intervene only for symptoms or when they cannot be told apart from lesions that may be malignant.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pregnancy:** complete surveillance before a planned conception where possible; any MRI during pregnancy is done without contrast, and no extra scans are needed if she stays well. An undiagnosed phaeochromocytoma is dangerous, especially in labour and delivery, so consider a high-risk pregnancy unit.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Genetics, Cancer Institute NSW, 'VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) disease – risk management (eviQ ID 397, version 11)', first approved 20 December 2010; last reviewed 13 May 2024; version 11 updated 23 February 2026; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/397, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **VHL-associated tumours belong with an experienced multidisciplinary team** that knows this disease.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First confirm the diagnosis of VHL disease:** a germline VHL alteration, or two or more hallmark VHL manifestations, or one hallmark manifestation plus a documented family history.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Belzutifan is for VHL tumours that do not need surgery now:** non-metastatic renal cell carcinoma, CNS haemangioblastoma, or non-metastatic pancreatic NET, in a patient with ECOG performance status 0-1.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In Australia the PBS funds belzutifan only for VHL-associated disease.** It is TGA-approved for pretreated advanced clear cell RCC (after a PD-1/L1 checkpoint inhibitor and VEGF-targeted therapy), but that use is not PBS-listed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily, continuously, until the disease progresses or toxicity becomes unacceptable.** Tablets are 40 mg.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose reductions go 120 → 80 → 40 mg once daily;** stop for good if the patient cannot manage after 2 reductions.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take it at about the same time each day, swallowed whole with water (not crushed or chewed), with or without food.** A missed dose can be taken later the same day; after vomiting, do not repeat the dose, just take the next one as usual.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nausea risk is minimal to low,** so routine antiemetic prophylaxis is not needed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Belzutifan can cause severe hypoxia** needing oxygen or admission. Onset is most often within the first 4 to 6 weeks, though it can appear months later. Check pulse oximetry before starting, regularly during that early window, then periodically.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypoxia at grade 3 (resting saturation 88% or less):** if symptomatic, withhold until grade 2 or better and restart one dose level lower or stop; **grade 4 (life-threatening airway compromise) means permanent discontinuation.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe anaemia from erythropoietin suppression is expected and may need transfusion,** usually within the first 3 months but sometimes much later. Patients with combined UGT2B17 and CYP2C19 deletions are at higher risk; genotyping is not routine but can be considered for unexplained severe anaemia.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Anaemia grade 1 to 2: carry on and correct iron, B12 or folate deficiency. Grade 3: withhold until grade 2 or better, then resume at the same or a lower dose. Grade 4: withhold, resume one level lower, and stop permanently if it recurs.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wounds heal poorly on belzutifan:** stop it at least 5 to 7 days before elective surgery and restart only once the wound has healed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other effects include fatigue, headache, dizziness, dyspnoea, joint and muscle pain, bowel upset, oedema, liver toxicity and hypertension;** control any existing hypertension before starting.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before starting, check a full blood count, kidney function (EUC, eGFR), liver tests, iron studies, B12 and folate.** Then consider repeating the blood count, kidney and liver tests fortnightly (every 2 weeks) for 6 weeks, monthly for the following 5 months, then 3-monthly.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No kidney dose change when eGFR is 30 or more;** below 30, and in moderate or severe liver impairment, use caution because these groups were not studied.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Belzutifan induces CYP3A4 and can make hormonal contraception fail;** anyone using it needs an added barrier method. Pregnancy testing should be considered before starting, and effective contraception is needed during and after treatment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CYP2C19 or UGT2B17 inhibitors (such as azoles, omeprazole, fluoxetine, ibuprofen) can raise belzutifan toxicity; CYP2C19 inducers (such as rifampicin or St John's wort) can reduce its effect.** Avoid these where possible or monitor closely.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The evidence is limited:** eviQ's committee published the protocol on the strength of the LITESPARK-004 single-arm, open-label phase 2 trial.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At a median follow-up of nearly 50 months, objective responses were 67% for VHL renal tumours (41 of 61), 48% for CNS haemangioblastomas (24 of 50) and 91% for pancreatic NETs (20 of 22).**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **All trial patients had some treatment-related side effect, and 18% had a grade 3 event;** anaemia and hypoxia were the key toxicities, and the one grade 3 hypoxia settled with interruption and dose reduction.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ESMO-MCBS score 3 out of 5** for VHL disease where local procedures are not immediately needed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4506 Belzutifan (eviQ ID 4506, version 2)', first approved 30 July 2025; version 2 published 13 April 2026; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4506, retrieved 2026-09-23
